# Snapsight: the full text of www.snapsight.com

> Snapsight is AI software for live events. One audio feed from each room gives every attendee live text, translation, key takeaways, an Idea Cloud and a summary on their own phone, from a QR code or link with no app. Afterwards, Remix turns the same sessions into post-event reports, sponsor reports and decks, and Speaker Remix gives each speaker a branded card and post to share. Live text translation is free for every event; voice translation is $10 per language per session, Engage is $299 per event, and Pro is $249 per session or from $99 in packs. Snapsight is headquartered in Singapore.

Plans, in USD before tax: Free ($0): live text translation in every room, up to 100 sessions a year. Engage ($299 per event): your branding, sponsor logos, Speaker Remix and Q&A moderation across one event. Pro ($249 per session of up to 2 hours), or packs of 20 for $3,980, 50 for $7,450, 100 for $9,900, used across events within 12 months; packs include Engage. Voice translation: $10 per language per session, on every plan. Extra Remix credits: 20 for $19. Enterprise: beyond 100 sessions a year, on request.

Generated 2026-10-09 from the published pages. Each page starts with its URL.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is live translation free for events?

Yes. Snapsight’s live text translation is free for every event, with no trial clock: every room at once, up to 10 languages per session from all 99, and 100 sessions a year. Attendees open a link or scan a QR code; there is no app. Voice translation, transcript downloads and Pro insights are paid.

### How do attendees get live translation on their phones without an app?

They scan the session’s QR code or open its link in their phone’s browser, then pick a language, and the speaker’s words appear in that language as they’re spoken. To listen instead of read, they use their own earbuds, so there are no headsets to rent and collect. Remote attendees open the same link wherever they are.

### What is the difference between reading along and listening?

Reading along shows the speaker’s words as live text in the attendee’s language, and it is free. Listening speaks them aloud in that language through the attendee’s own earbuds, in the same 99 languages, at $10 per language, per session, with captions for that language included.

### How many languages can one session be translated into?

Up to 10 per session, chosen from 99, and each attendee picks one on their own phone. The full list, with native names, is on Snapsight’s live translation page. Voice translation is charged for each language you turn on for listening.

### How accurate is AI live translation at a conference?

Snapsight’s English transcription is 97% accurate, measured on English sessions with a direct feed from the venue mixer; speech is recognised in about 200 ms and the translated text follows as each phrase forms. Accuracy varies with audio quality, accents and language. Take the feed from the sound desk and add speaker names, sponsor brands and acronyms as custom vocabulary before the session.

### Can AI translation replace interpreters at a conference?

It covers the sessions interpreters usually don’t. Events use Snapsight for every session that never had interpreters, such as breakouts, workshops and show-floor stages, and some keep interpreters for a flagship keynote. Interpreters remain the better choice for high-stakes sessions where certified accuracy and cultural nuance matter most, such as legal or diplomatic settings.

### What happens when a speaker switches languages mid-sentence?

Snapsight follows them. When a speaker moves between languages, even within a sentence, the live text keeps up on its own, and each attendee still reads in the language they picked.

### What does our AV team need for live translation?

One audio feed: the room’s mixer output sent to a laptop running Snapsight, with a reliable internet connection. Put the session’s QR code on the stage screen, a slide or a badge. Snapsight’s team checks the feed, languages and attendee access with you before doors open.

### Can we translate several rooms at the same time?

Free covers every room at once, so breakouts and side stages get the same translation as the main stage: one audio feed and one QR code each. The $299 Engage event pass adds your branding, sponsor logos and Q&A moderation across all of them, and larger programmes talk to Snapsight about Enterprise.

### Can attendees keep the translated transcript afterwards?

Free is for following live. Transcript downloads, summaries and live takeaways come with Snapsight Pro at $249 per session of up to 2 hours, or from $99 a session in packs.

## Captions, subtitles, transcripts. Here’s what each one is.

Four ways to read a talk, and one way to hear it in another language.

Live captions, translated captions, voice and transcripts

| | What it is | With Snapsight |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Live captions | The speaker’s words as text, in the language they are speaking, as they speak. | Free for every event, on each attendee’s phone. |
| Translated captions | Sometimes called live subtitles: the same words translated into another language as they are spoken. | Free as live text translation, up to 10 languages per session. |
| Voice translation | The talk spoken aloud in another language, through the attendee’s own earbuds. | $10 per language per session, with captions included. |
| Room-screen captions | The live text shown full screen on a stage display, TV or monitor, for everyone in the room. | Presentation Mode: high contrast, readable at a distance. |
| Transcript | The full text of the session, to keep and search afterwards. | Transcript and subtitle downloads with Pro, $249 per session or less in packs. |

Real session text · Henry Coutinho-Mason · IMEX Frankfurt 2025

## One captioner, one room. AI captions in every room.

Choose per session. Many events need both.

A human captioner, often called CART (Communication Access Realtime Translation), writes every word live and is booked for each session in advance. Book one when an attendee asks for a human captioner, or for a session where every word needs a person’s check.

AI captions make captions the default for every breakout and side stage, not only the keynote.

[What CART captioning is, and what it costs](https://www.snapsight.com/en/resources/glossary/cart-services/)

### Human captioner (CART)

A trained captioner writes them live. One captioner or team per room, booked in advance for each session, usually in the language spoken on stage.

Best for requested accommodations and sessions that need a human check.

### Snapsight live captions

AI writes them from the room’s audio feed, in every room that has one, all at once. Turned on per session and free for every event, in the spoken language or translated into the attendee’s.

Best for every session, for anyone who follows better by reading.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I add live captions to a conference?

Send each room’s audio from the mixer to a laptop running Snapsight and put the session’s QR code on screen. Attendees scan it and read live captions on their own phones as the speaker talks. Snapsight’s team checks the feed with you before doors open.

### Can attendees get live captions on their own phones without an app?

Yes. They scan the session’s QR code or open its link in their phone’s browser, and Snapsight’s captions appear as the speaker talks. There is nothing to download and no devices to hand out.

### Can we show live captions on the screen in the room?

Yes. Presentation Mode puts the live text full screen on a stage display, TV or monitor, in a high-contrast layout made for reading at a distance. Use it in the main room, in overflow rooms or on digital signage, while each attendee can still follow on their own phone.

### Are live captions free?

Yes. Snapsight’s live captions and text translation are free for every event: every room at once, up to 10 languages per session, and 100 sessions a year. The $299 Engage pass puts your branding and sponsor logos on the captions, and transcript downloads come with Pro.

### How accurate are AI live captions?

Snapsight’s English transcription is 97% accurate, measured on English sessions with a direct feed from the venue mixer, and speech becomes text in about 200 ms. Accuracy varies with audio quality, accents and language, so take the feed from the sound desk and add names and acronyms as custom vocabulary.

### What is the difference between captions and subtitles?

Captions show the speaker’s words in the language they are speaking; subtitles translate them into another language. Snapsight gives attendees both live: captions in the spoken language, or translated captions in the language each attendee picks.

### What is CART captioning, and when do we still need it?

CART (Communication Access Realtime Translation) is live captioning by a trained human captioner, booked per session. Book it when an attendee asks for a human captioner, or for a session where every word needs a person’s check. Snapsight’s AI captions can cover every other session, in every room with an audio feed.

### Can live captions be translated into other languages?

Yes. Each attendee picks a language on their own phone and reads the captions translated as the speaker talks, with up to 10 languages per session. To hear the translation instead, voice is $10 per language per session, with captions included.

### Will captions get speaker names and technical terms right?

Add speaker names, sponsor brands, drug names and acronyms as custom vocabulary before the session, and they come out right on every phone. Speaker detection shows who is talking on panels, and Snapsight keeps up when a speaker switches languages mid-sentence.

### Can we download the captions as a transcript or subtitle file?

Yes, with Snapsight Pro. Transcript and subtitle downloads are included for purchased Pro sessions at $249 per session of up to 2 hours, less in packs; Free and Engage are for following live.

Title: AI Session Summaries & Live Takeaways for Events | Snapsight

Live takeaways and AI session summaries

# Let Snapsight take the notes.

Key takeaways land on every attendee’s phone while the speaker is still talking, and a session summary follows, in their language.

[Book a demo](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/contact?interest=takeaways) [Try the real session](https://www.snapsight.com/live-channel/6ec65ea8-b74c-4e27-bf85-78f2b1496a6d/427cfb00-b6c1-4ddf-9eae-e66ccabc9f3a/attendee?tab=takeaways)

**40:00** / 40:00

Talk ended · 9 takeaways, 8 ideas and a summary

**Thriving in the AI era** *🇬🇧 English*

Summary

At IMEX Frankfurt 2025, Henry Coutinho-Mason delivered a thought-provoking presentation titled "Thriving in the AI era: Non-obvious ways to design a people-first AI strategy." Challenging the fetishization of AI technology, he echoed Jeff Bezos' focus on unchanging human needs in events: connection, learning, and creation. Coutinho-Mason showcased AI's potential through diverse examples, from Microsoft's multimodal AI for real-time coaching to Salesforce's AI sales coach, introducing the concept of an AI-powered meeting copilot to enhance event experiences.

The speaker illustrated human-AI collaboration using chess examples of Garry Kasparov and Magnus Carlsen. For networking, he presented Bawdy, an AI tool for meaningful event introductions, contrasting it with Mark Zuckerberg's virtual friends concept. Coutinho-Mason envisioned AI enhancing real-time event Q&A and even demonstrated an AI-generated event soundtrack.

Real session · Henry Coutinho-Mason · IMEX Frankfurt 2025

## Frequently asked questions

### What are live takeaways?

Live takeaways are the key points of a talk, written by Snapsight as the speaker makes them and shown on every attendee’s phone. Each is a short headline and a sentence or two, usually around ten per session, and links back to the speaker’s own words. Attendees also get an Idea Cloud of the session’s themes and a summary afterwards.

### How soon do takeaways appear during a session?

As the talk goes: Snapsight adds each takeaway as the speaker makes the point, so the list builds during the session. At Festival of Curiosity, takeaways appeared four to five minutes into each session. The summary is ready straight after the session ends.

### What is an Idea Cloud?

The Idea Cloud is a live map of a session’s themes, built by Snapsight from what the speaker says, and it grows as the talk goes. Attendees tap a theme to see its takeaway and the speaker’s own words. Organisers can put it on the main screen, LED walls or foyer screens, in the event’s colours.

### How accurate are AI session summaries?

Snapsight writes takeaways and summaries from the stage audio, and every idea links back to the words that were said, with the speaker’s name on them, so anyone can check the source. Speaker detection keeps names right on panels, and quality follows the audio, so take a direct feed from the sound desk. The attendee view notes that AI-generated content may contain mistakes.

### How are takeaways different from a transcript?

A transcript is every word; takeaways are the points worth keeping. Snapsight gives attendees both during the session: live text of what is said, and around ten takeaways that build as the speaker makes each point. Full transcript downloads come with Pro.

### What do we need on site for live takeaways?

One audio feed from your sound desk, and the session’s QR code on screen or in print. Snapsight tests the feed and your languages with you before doors open.

### Do attendees need an app to see the takeaways?

No. Each session has a link and a QR code that open in the phone’s browser, with the live text, takeaways, Idea Cloud and summary in the language the attendee chooses. Takeaways can also sit inside your event app, as they did in the FIP Congress App at FIP’s 2025 World Congress.

### Which languages are the takeaways in?

99, for reading and listening. Each attendee picks their own language on their own phone, and the takeaways, Idea Cloud and summary follow it.

### How much do AI session summaries cost?

Snapsight Pro is $249 per session of up to 2 hours, or $199, $149 and $99 a session in packs of 20, 50 and 100, valid for 12 months. Pro includes live takeaways, the Idea Cloud, summaries, transcript downloads, Remix for post-event content, and MCP and API access; packs also include Engage for every event they are used at. Live text translation stays free.

### Can takeaways from a closed session stay private?

Yes. Add an access code to the session, and only people with the code can open its live text, takeaways and summary. Your content stays yours and is never used to train AI models.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I turn conference sessions into a post-event report?

Capture the sessions with Snapsight, then ask Remix for the report: say who it’s for and what it should cover, such as the themes across every stage with the quotes behind them. Remix drafts it from the sessions you pick, and you ask for changes until it’s right. Festival of Curiosity’s bilingual reports were generated automatically from its sessions.

### What can Remix make from event sessions?

Post-event reports, sponsor reports, LinkedIn carousels, one-pagers, decks, and versions in your audience’s language. If you can describe it, Snapsight’s Remix drafts it from your sessions, which makes it a quick way to repurpose conference content for marketing, members and sponsors.

### What does Remix work from?

Only the sessions you pick: their takeaways, quotes and transcripts, with speaker names and session details already attached. That can be one session, a track, a day or the whole programme.

### How do we check a Remix report is accurate?

Every quote in a Remix draft carries a speaker and a session, so your team can trace it back before anything is published. If something isn’t right, say so and Remix updates the draft.

### Can Remix follow our brand and editorial style?

Yes. Give Remix the tone, length, colours and sponsor logos in the brief, or ask for plain text to drop into your own templates.

### Can we make a sponsor report from our sessions?

Yes. Ask Remix for a sponsor report and put the sponsor’s logo in the brief; reports for The Meetings Show Asia Pacific 2024 and AIME 2025 carried their partners. Snapsight’s sponsorship page has two packages you can sell around it.

### Can we pull Remix content into our CMS or AI tools?

Yes. Pull takeaways and reports into your CMS over the Snapsight API, or connect your own AI assistant to your sessions over MCP.

### How much does Remix cost?

Each Snapsight Pro session ($249) includes 5 Remix credits, the 20-, 50- and 100-session packs include 100, 250 and 500, and an extra 20 credits cost $19. One credit creates one new standard text output; downloads and manual edits use no credits.

### Is our content safe in Remix?

Snapsight is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified, and GDPR compliant. Your content is never used to train AI models, your data, and the IP in it, belongs to you, and Remix works only from the sessions you choose.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I get speakers to share our event on LinkedIn?

Give them something worth posting from their own talk. With Snapsight’s Speaker Remix, each speaker gets a private link, picks three takeaways from their session and gets a card in your event’s design plus a draft post they can edit. London Community Week made a card for all 49 speakers and shared them in 147 official LinkedIn posts across three Pages.

### What is a speaker card?

A branded image with one point from the speaker’s own session, their name, role and company, and your event’s name, dates and colours, with sponsor marks if you sell them. Speaker Remix makes one for each speaker from the session’s takeaways, alongside a draft post.

### Does anything publish without the speaker choosing to share?

No. The speaker selects the takeaways, reviews the card and draft post, and decides what to share. Opening a LinkedIn draft does not publish it.

### Does the content come from the actual session?

Yes. Speaker Remix starts from the takeaways Snapsight captured in the speaker’s own session, so the card uses the words they said. Speakers review the card and the post before anything is shared.

### Can the card carry our event identity and sponsors?

Yes. The London Community Week cards carry the event’s name, dates, colours and sponsor marks. Snapsight reviews your event’s assets and formats with you in a demo.

### How much work is it for our team?

One link per speaker. Your team captures the sessions, adds your logo, colours and sponsor marks, and shares each speaker’s private link; the speaker chooses the takeaways, reviews the card and edits the post. There is no design work for your team and no chasing speakers for posts.

### How do speakers get to their content?

Your team shares each speaker’s private link. They choose their takeaways, create the card and review the post on their own device, then download it or open a LinkedIn draft.

### How is Speaker Remix different from Remix?

Remix is for your team’s reports, posts and decks. Speaker Remix gives each speaker a focused way to turn their own session into a card and a post they want to share.

### Which Snapsight plan includes Speaker Remix?

Engage includes the Speaker Remix workflow, with generation using Remix credits. Each Pro session also includes an automatic speaker content kit, a session recap, social posts, suggested quotes and a follow-up email, that uses no credits.

Title: How It Works: Live Translation Setup at Events | Snapsight

How it works · Setup for translation and takeaways

# One audio feed and one QR code. That’s the whole setup.

Your AV team sends the room audio to a laptop. We check it with you before doors open.

[Book a setup call](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/contact?interest=setup) [Start free](https://www.snapsight.com/signup)

## Before the event, a sound check with us.

Set up languages and names, then test the audio together.

1. **Turn on your languages** Up to 10 per session, from 99. Each attendee picks one.
2. **Add your vocabulary** Speaker names, sponsor brands and acronyms, so they come out right on every phone.
3. **Put up the QR code** Each session has its own link and QR code, for the stage screen, a slide, a badge or print.
4. **Run the sound check with us** We check the feed, your languages and attendee access with you before doors open.

![Close-up of the Snapsight capture screen on a laptop, with Leave Session, Sound Check and Stop Live Capture buttons](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/assets/audio-feed-laptop-Bf7GySzn.webp)

The Snapsight laptop beside the stage at IMEX Frankfurt

## In the room, one feed from the sound desk.

Your AV team sends the mixer feed to a laptop running Snapsight, with a reliable internet connection. That’s the whole install.

1. ### Connect your audio.

   From your venue’s mixer or an online session.
2. Listening to your session

   ### Let Snapsight listen.

   Live text, translation and insights from the same feed.
3. Your session

   Live

   Live text

   Key takeaways

   Idea Cloud

   Summary

   Q&A

   ### Share one QR code.

   Attendees scan and follow along. No app to download.

## Talk through your setup before your next event.

Or start free: live text and translation are free for every event.

## Frequently asked questions

### What equipment do we need for live translation at an event?

A laptop running Snapsight in each room, the room’s audio from the mixer, and a reliable internet connection. Attendees use their own phones, so there are no booths, consoles or headsets. Each session has its own QR code for the stage screen, a slide, a badge or print.

### Do attendees need an app?

No. They scan the QR code or open the session link in their phone’s browser, then pick a language. To listen rather than read, they use their own earbuds.

### Who runs Snapsight on the day?

Your AV team connects the feed and puts up the QR code, and Snapsight’s team checks the feed, languages and attendee access with you before doors open. CityDNA captured 15+ sessions with no one monitoring them.

### How long does setup take?

WiT Japan & North Asia 2024 went from start to live within a week, with one person handling AV, setup and integration. On the day, each room needs one audio feed and one QR code.

### What if the audio is poor?

Accuracy follows the audio, the accent and the language. Snapsight’s 97% English accuracy is measured with a direct feed from the venue mixer, so take the feed from the sound desk and use the sound check to hear it before doors open. Custom vocabulary keeps names, brands and acronyms right.

### Can Snapsight run in several rooms at once?

Free covers every room at once, up to 100 sessions a year. The $299 Engage event pass lifts that cap for the event and adds your branding, sponsor logos and Q&A moderation; for larger programmes Snapsight prices Enterprise with you.

### Does it work for online and hybrid sessions?

Yes. Snapsight can take the audio from an online session as well as from a venue mixer, and remote attendees open the same session link as the room.

### We already have recordings. Can we use them?

Yes. Upload a recording to Snapsight for takeaways, summaries and Remix.

### What happens after the session?

Takeaways and summaries stay open, so people who missed a session can catch up. Remix drafts post-event and sponsor reports, carousels and decks from your sessions, and each speaker gets a private Speaker Remix link for a card and a draft post.

### Where does the audio from our sound desk go?

To Snapsight, encrypted in transit and at rest and hosted in Frankfurt, Germany, by default. Snapsight is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified, and GDPR compliant. Your content never trains AI models, and your data, and the IP in it, belongs to you.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can Snapsight work inside Cvent, Swapcard or our event app?

Yes. Snapsight works inside any event app that can embed a web page or open a link, including Swapcard, Cvent, Bizzabo, Whova, Grip, Brella, EventsAir, Hubilo, EventMobi and Stova. FIP ran it in its congress app, and IMEX, ICCA and UFI in theirs.

### Is it a formal integration with those apps?

It doesn’t need one. Snapsight uses what event apps already support: embedding a web page or opening a link. Identiverse 2024 linked to its session reports from its own event app, and UFI’s tech team added takeaways to its conference app themselves, with no code.

### Which parts of Snapsight can we embed in our app?

The session views: live text, takeaways, Idea Cloud and summary. Every session has its own link, the same one behind its QR code, and there is one link for the whole event.

### Will attendees be sent out of the app?

Not if you embed it. If you use a link, your app team allows the Snapsight link, and most apps then open it in their own in-app browser.

### Does Snapsight work for sessions on Zoom, Teams and Google Meet?

Yes. Snapsight takes the audio from online sessions on Zoom, Microsoft Teams and Google Meet, and remote attendees open the same session link as the room to follow live text in their language.

### Which identity providers do you support for SSO?

Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD), Okta and other identity providers, for your team’s sign-in. Single sign-on is part of Snapsight Enterprise, alongside team administration.

### Does Snapsight have an API or an MCP server?

Yes. Pull takeaways and summaries into your own systems over the Snapsight API, or connect your own AI assistant to your sessions over MCP and ask it about any session.

### What if we don’t have an event app?

Attendees don’t need one. Without an event app, they scan the session’s QR code or open its link in their phone’s browser.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much does Snapsight cost?

Live text translation is free for every event, in every room, up to 100 sessions a year. The Engage event pass is $299; Pro is $249 per session of up to 2 hours, or $199, $149 and $99 a session in packs of 20, 50 and 100; voice translation is $10 per language per session. Programmes of more than 100 sessions a year price below $99 as Enterprise, and all prices are in USD before tax.

### What is included in the free plan?

Live transcription and text translation in every room at once, with up to 10 active text languages from the full supported catalogue and 100 sessions a year. Free includes live viewing with Snapsight branding, basic Q&A and manual polls, and the session count is always in view. Voice translation, transcript downloads and Pro insights are paid.

### What counts as a session?

A session is up to 2 hours, and a longer session counts as two: it uses two Pro sessions from a pack, costs $20 per voice language, and takes two of the free 100. An Engage event covers every room and session of that event, with all presenters. There is no per-attendee fee.

### What happens after 100 free sessions in a year?

The next session needs an Engage pass for its event, at $299, or a Pro pack. Sessions in an Engage or Pro event never count towards the 100, a session that is already live is never stopped, and the count resets each year.

### Do I need Engage and Pro?

A Pro pack includes Engage for every event it is used at, so your branding, sponsor logos, Speaker Remix and Q&A moderation run in every room of those events. A single Pro session covers that session only. Choose Engage on its own when you want the event experience without takeaways, transcripts or Remix.

### How much does voice translation cost?

Voice translation is an optional $10 per language per session on every plan, including Free, and each paid voice language includes its text captions. Three languages across five sessions of up to 2 hours cost $150. Voice does not unlock Pro transcript downloads or insights.

### Can I download transcripts with Free or Engage?

No. Transcript and subtitle downloads are included only for purchased Pro sessions, including Pro sessions in Enterprise. Engage adds Speaker Remix cards, engagement analytics and exports of questions and poll results, not the full spoken transcript.

### Do attendees or speakers have to pay?

No. Attendees join by link or QR code without buying a plan to view what you have enabled. Speakers get their Speaker Remix cards on Engage and Pro events without a subscription of their own.

### Is there a discount for nonprofits, associations or education?

Yes. Snapsight offers special pricing for nonprofits, associations, education and larger events, and Enterprise includes volume rates and wholesale options for AV and production partners. The public prices are the most you’ll pay, in USD before tax.

Title: Event Translation Cost Calculator | Snapsight

# What translating your event costs, with interpreters and with Snapsight.

Set your agenda. Interpreter figures use published rates, listed below.

Format

Human interpreters **$25,320–$39,560**

- 12 interpreters × 2 days $13,560–$22,560
- AV technician, 2 rooms $1,400–$4,000
- Booths, 3 languages × 2 rooms $3,360–$6,000
- Headsets, 500 × $7 a day $7,000

Snapsight **$360**

- Live text, 3 languages Free
- Voice, 3 languages × 12 sessions × $10 $360

Difference for the same 12 sessions: **$24,960–$39,200**

[Discuss this estimate](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/contact?interest=voice-translation&sessions=12&attendees=500&languages=3&estimate=360&currency=USD) [Start free](https://www.snapsight.com/signup)

USD, before tax. Interpreter figures exclude travel, per diems and agency fees. More than 10 rooms or 7 days? [Ask for a quote](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/contact?interest=enterprise).

Attendees read or listen on their own phones.

## Where every figure comes from.

Institutional rates, so a private interpreter quote usually runs higher.

### Snapsight

**Live text translation**

Free, in every language

**Voice translation**

$10 per language per session of up to 2 hours

**Parallel rooms**

Free, every room: one audio feed and one QR code each

[See pricing](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/pricing)

### Human interpretation

**Interpreters per language**

Two per booth, rotating every 20–30 minutes[AIIC standards, Art. 6–7](https://aiic.org/document/9809/AIIC%20Italia_Professional%20standards_2021.pdf) [AIIC Switzerland](https://aiic.ch/about-interpreting/)

**Interpreter day rate**

$565–$940[UN system rates](https://unsceb.org/2025-interpreters-rates) [EU–AIIC agreement](https://aiic.org/document/9550/EU-AIIC_Agreement_Rates_EN.pdf) [US Courts](https://www.uscourts.gov/court-programs/federal-court-interpreters)

**Interpreter working day**

Two sessions of 2.5–3 hours. Agenda items assumed at 90 minutes.[AIIC standards, Art. 8](https://aiic.org/document/9809/AIIC%20Italia_Professional%20standards_2021.pdf)

**Booths and headsets**

$280–$500 per language per room a day; $7 per attendee a day[Equipment rate card](https://latranslation.com/interpreters/interpreting-equipment-rental/) [ISO 4043](https://www.iso.org/standard/67066.html)

**AV technician**

$350–$1,000 a day, per room[Vendor rate card](https://latranslation.com/interpreters/interpreting-equipment-rental/) [Cornell AV rates](https://it.cornell.edu/av-installation/audio-visual-installation-consulting-and-engineering-rates-and-fees)

## Translate every session, not just the keynote.

Live text is free. Add voice where your audience needs it.

[Book a demo](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/contact?interest=voice-translation) [Start free](https://www.snapsight.com/signup)

## Frequently asked questions

### What’s the cheapest way to translate a conference into 10 languages?

Live text translation: with Snapsight it is free in up to 10 languages per session, read on attendees’ own phones, in every room at once. If attendees need to hear the translation, voice is $10 per language per session, so 10 languages across 12 sessions costs $1,200. Interpreters for the same coverage need at least two per language per booth.

### How much does simultaneous interpretation cost?

Professional simultaneous interpretation needs at least two interpreters per language per booth. Published institutional day rates run about $565 to $940 per interpreter: UN system AIIC-agreement rates are USD 557–836, the EU–AIIC agreement is EUR 632, and US Courts pay $566 for a certified full day. Private conference work is quoted higher. Add a technician at roughly $350 to $1,000 a day, booths at about $280 to $500 per language per day, and headsets at about $7 per attendee per day.

### How many interpreters does a conference need?

At least two per language per booth, rotating every 20 to 30 minutes, per AIIC professional standards. An interpreter’s working day is capped at two sessions of two and a half to three hours, so a dense agenda or parallel tracks need more teams.

### What does Snapsight cost for the same event?

Live text translation is free in every language. Voice translation, heard through attendees’ own earbuds, is $10 per language per session of up to 2 hours. Free covers every room at once, and there is no per-attendee fee.

### When should we still book interpreters?

For flagship, high-stakes sessions where certified accuracy and cultural nuance matter most, such as legal or diplomatic settings. Many events keep interpreters for a main keynote and use Snapsight for every other session.

### What does the estimate leave out?

Interpreter travel, accommodation, per diems, overtime, agency fees, recording rights and cancellation terms, and every one of them makes the human figure higher. Real quotes vary by market, vendor and lead time.

## Send us your stage plan. We’ll show you what each stage gets.

Tell us your stages and days, and we’ll show you what attendees and sponsors get.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do we capture every seminar theatre at a trade show?

Give each stage one audio feed from its sound desk and put its QR code on the stage screen. Snapsight then gives attendees live text, translation and takeaways from every stage at once. Tech Week Singapore 2024 put QR codes on all 17 stages, and ATxEnterprise ran all five.

### Can attendees on the show floor catch sessions they missed?

Yes. Takeaways and summaries stay available, so attendees in meetings or on the floor can read the sessions they missed. At Tech Week Singapore 2024, 26,000+ attendees got the takeaways from sessions they couldn’t reach. At The Meetings Show 2025, every attendee got all 65 sessions, up from the 8–10 one person could attend.

### Our theatres are on the show floor. Does the noise matter?

Accuracy follows the audio, so take a direct feed from each stage’s sound desk rather than a room microphone. Snapsight checks every feed with you before doors open.

### Do attendees need to download anything?

No. They scan the QR code or open the link in their phone’s browser, as ATxEnterprise attendees did at all five stages. Or put the takeaways inside your show app.

### Can exhibitors and visitors follow sessions in their own language?

Yes. Each attendee picks a language on their own phone and reads the session as live text, free for every event. Listening to a translated voice through their own earbuds costs $10 per language, per session.

### Can we make reports for our sponsors?

Yes. Remix drafts post-event and sponsor reports from the sessions you pick, and the brief can carry your sponsors’ logos. AIME 2025’s report carried its partners on the cover.

### Will we know which sessions people cared about?

Yes. At Tech Week Singapore 2024, organisers saw which sessions drew the most interest: 13,773 views from 1,540 active users.

### What does Snapsight cost for a trade show?

Live text translation is free for every event, in every room. The $299 Engage event pass adds your branding, sponsor logos and Q&A moderation for the whole event; takeaways and reports come with Pro at $249 per session, less in packs; and bigger shows talk to Snapsight about Enterprise.

## Send us your programme. We’ll show you what attendees get.

Tell us about your rooms and tracks, and we’ll take you through a real session.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does Snapsight handle medical and technical terms?

Yes, when you add them first. Drug names, trial acronyms and speaker names go in as custom vocabulary before the event. ARC APAC Summit ran it across 20+ jargon-heavy healthcare sessions for 300+ professionals, and 40% of attendees used it.

### How accurate is Snapsight at a conference?

Accuracy follows the audio, the accent and the language. Snapsight’s 97% English accuracy is measured with a direct feed from the venue mixer, so take the feed from the sound desk and use the sound check to hear it before doors open. Custom vocabulary keeps names, brands and acronyms right.

### Can our team correct a takeaway?

Yes. Takeaways can be edited as they come in: at Festival of Curiosity, one person started each session and another edited in real time. Remix reports can be edited too, and manual edits use no credits.

### What do we need on site?

One audio feed and one QR code per room. Send the room audio from the mixer to a laptop running Snapsight, with a reliable internet connection, and Snapsight checks the feed with you before doors open. At WiT Japan & North Asia 2024, one person ran AV, setup and integration.

### How soon is the session summary ready?

Straight after each session, by QR code. Economist Impact had highlights out the same day at AI Innovation Asia 2024, where edited recordings could take up to 48 hours.

### Can we cover parallel tracks?

Yes. Each room needs one audio feed and one QR code, and Free covers every room at once. Attendees can follow one session live and read the takeaways from another.

### Can attendees follow in their own language?

Yes, in 99 languages, each attendee on their own phone. Reading along is free; listening costs $10 per language, per session. At FIP’s 2025 World Congress, attendees could open real-time translations of every congress presentation in the FIP Congress App.

### Can we get a report on just one track?

Yes. One session, a track, a day or the whole programme: Remix works only from the sessions you pick, and every quote carries its speaker and session. The Decarbonised Mine finished its post-event reports over a weekend instead of weeks.

### Where does our session data go?

Snapsight is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified, and GDPR compliant. Your content never trains AI models, your data, and the IP in it, belongs to you, and data is hosted in Frankfurt by default.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do we give members who couldn’t attend the content from our congress?

Capture every session with Snapsight and share the takeaways, summaries and a post-event report afterwards. AICPA & CIMA had Snapsight draft the report of a two-day advisory group meeting, and ICCA sent attendees a full report built from its 2024 congress. Remix drafts more formats from the same sessions, such as a member newsletter or a one-pager.

### Can the takeaways sit inside our conference app?

Yes. FIP put them in its congress app for every presentation, and UFI’s own tech team added them to its app with no code. Or use a QR code and a link that opens in the browser.

### We’re a small team. Who runs it on the day?

CityDNA’s organising team of four captured 15+ sessions with no one monitoring. At BEIA, one volunteer ran it after a 15-minute test at home.

### Will attendees actually use it?

CityDNA printed the QR code on every badge and reached 65% of attendees. 40% of PCMA Convening Leaders attendees used it, and 60%+ at ICCA Congress engaged with it in the app.

### What do we get after the conference?

A report built from the sessions. CityDNA’s team saved hours, maybe days, of post-event work, and UFI uses its report, with sentiment analysis, in strategic planning. Remix drafts more formats from the same sessions.

### Can members follow in their own language?

Yes. CityDNA ran live multilingual translation across 15+ sessions, and PCMA ran takeaways in seven languages. Live text translation is free in up to 10 of 99 languages per session.

### Do you offer association or nonprofit pricing?

Yes. Snapsight offers special pricing for nonprofits, associations, education and larger events. Live text translation is free for every event either way.

### Is our content safe?

Snapsight is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified, and GDPR compliant. Your content never trains AI models, and your data, and the IP in it, belongs to you, transcripts and summaries included.

## Mostly volunteers? Fifteen minutes to learn it.

What it took at Festival of Curiosity, run by two, and at BEIA, run by one volunteer.

1. ### Before

   One try-out. The festival team rehearsed in its office; BEIA’s organiser tested it at home.
2. ### On the day

   One or two people. At the festival, one person started sessions and another edited; a volunteer ran every BEIA session.
3. ### In the room

   A QR code and a word from the MC. BEIA showed the code at the entrances and in the breaks, and the MC explained it each morning.

What each room needs: one audio feed and one QR code.

## Tell us about your festival. We’ll show you what visitors get.

Live text translation is free for every event, so you can start with one session.

## Frequently asked questions

### We’re mostly volunteers. How many people does it take?

One or two. Two ran Festival of Curiosity’s 130+ activities: one started sessions, the other edited in real time. One volunteer ran BEIA’s conference with Snapsight.

### Can we run it with no AV team?

Yes. At WiT Japan & North Asia 2024, one person handled the AV, the setup and the integration. Each room needs its sound sent to a laptop running Snapsight, with a reliable internet connection.

### How do attendees find it?

By QR code. CityDNA printed it on every badge and reached 65% of attendees. BEIA showed it on the entrance screens and in the breaks, put it on table sheets and in the conference app, and the MC explained it each morning.

### Our speakers switch languages mid-sentence. Does that work?

Yes. Snapsight follows a speaker who switches language mid-sentence. Festival of Curiosity ran German and English, Austrian dialect included.

### Can attendees read in another language?

Yes, each on their own phone. GSTC2025, the Global Sustainable Tourism Conference in Fiji, offered multilingual summaries to delegates from more than 40 countries.

### How do speakers share their session?

Each speaker gets a private Speaker Remix link, chooses their takeaways and reviews the card and the post. Nothing is shared until they choose to share it.

### What’s free for community events?

Live text translation for every event: every room at once, up to 10 languages per session, and 100 sessions a year. Takeaways, reports and Speaker Remix are paid.

### Do visitors need an app?

No. They scan the QR code and read in their browser.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does Snapsight work for a leadership meeting, not just a conference?

Yes. AICPA & CIMA used it at a two-day meeting of its Future of Finance Leadership Advisory Group, CFOs and senior finance executives from Fortune 500 and Global 1000 companies, and Snapsight drafted the meeting’s report.

### Do we get a finished report?

You get a draft built from what was said, and your team finishes it. AICPA & CIMA’s team edited theirs and confirmed quote attributions with the members.

### Can different audiences get their own report?

Yes. The Singapore Apex Business Summit 2024 had a summary after each day, then separate reports for the Ministry of Trade and Industry, the Ministry of Manpower, private-sector business leaders and the maritime and logistics sector.

### Can Snapsight cover every breakout, not just the main stage?

Yes. Identiverse 2024 put a QR code at each session and had insights for all 250+ sessions over four days.

### Do attendees need another app?

No. They scan the session’s QR code and read in their browser. Identiverse also announced it, and the session reports, in its own event app.

### Where does our content go?

Snapsight is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified, and GDPR compliant. Your content never trains AI models, and your data, and the IP in it, belongs to you, transcripts and summaries included.

### What does Snapsight cost for a corporate event?

Live text translation is free for every event, in every room. The $299 Engage event pass adds your branding, sponsor logos and Q&A moderation, and takeaways, summaries and transcripts come with Pro at $249 per session, less in packs.

## Frequently asked questions

### What new sponsorship can we sell at a conference?

Sponsorship of the content itself. With Snapsight, a sponsor can present the takeaways, Idea Clouds and summaries from every session, and the post-event reports attendees come back to, with their logo on screens, in the app, on reports and on speaker cards. You sell it in your own tiers, at your price.

### Where can a sponsor’s logo appear?

On the walk-in and QR slides, on the stage screen, in your event app, on report covers and pages, on a sponsor page inside the report, and on speaker cards and decks. The slides read “Educational Summaries presented by” your sponsor, and report pages read “Post-Event Insights presented by” them.

### Who sells the sponsorship, and who sets the price?

You do. It sits in your own sponsorship programme, at the price you set, and Snapsight delivers the placements.

### How should we price sponsored summaries and reports?

Against your existing tiers. Snapsight’s guidance is to price it above a logo placement of similar prominence, because the sponsor stays in view long after the event ends.

### How can we package it?

As a premium add-on, as part of your Gold, Platinum or custom tiers, or as an exclusive for a single sponsor. One sponsor can take the whole event, or you can sell a different one for each room, stage or track.

### Does the sponsor change the content?

No. Takeaways and reports come from what was said on stage, and the sponsor presents them. Their own message goes on their sponsor page, if you sell one.

### Do you have wording for our prospectus?

Yes. Copy the Educational Summaries Sponsorship or the Post-Event Content & Reports Sponsorship from this page, then add your sponsor’s name and your standard benefits. Snapsight helps you fit them into your tiers on a call.

AI-generated content may contain mistakes.

Real takeaways and summary · Henry Coutinho-Mason · IMEX Frankfurt 2025. The minutes are illustrative.

After the session

Summary

At IMEX Frankfurt 2025, Henry Coutinho-Mason delivered a thought-provoking presentation titled "Thriving in the AI era: Non-obvious ways to design a people-first AI strategy." Challenging the fetishization of AI technology, he echoed Jeff Bezos' focus on unchanging human needs in events: connection, learning, and creation. Coutinho-Mason showcased AI's potential through diverse examples, from Microsoft's multimodal AI for real-time coaching to Salesforce's AI sales coach, introducing the concept of an AI-powered meeting copilot to enhance event experiences.

The speaker illustrated human-AI collaboration using chess examples of Garry Kasparov and Magnus Carlsen. For networking, he presented Bawdy, an AI tool for meaningful event introductions, contrasting it with Mark Zuckerberg's virtual friends concept. Coutinho-Mason envisioned AI enhancing real-time event Q&A and even demonstrated an AI-generated event soundtrack.

## Bring one session. We’ll show you every way in.

We set up captions, languages and takeaways with you, and test them before doors open.

[Book an accessibility demo](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/contact?interest=accessibility) [Start free](https://www.snapsight.com/signup)

## Frequently asked questions

### Does Snapsight help attendees who are deaf or hard of hearing?

Yes. Live captions appear on their own phone as the speaker talks, and the text stays on the page so they can read back. Speaker detection shows who is talking on panels, and custom vocabulary keeps names and terms right.

### Can captions go on the stage screen as well as on phones?

Yes. Presentation Mode shows the live text full screen on a stage display or monitor, high-contrast and readable at a distance, so attendees who are hard of hearing can follow without looking down. Everyone can still read along on their own phone.

### Does Snapsight work for neurodivergent attendees?

Each attendee chooses how to follow: live text at their own pace, takeaways that build as the talk goes, the Idea Cloud, or the summary afterwards, and they can step out and catch up. Snapsight doesn’t claim one format suits everyone; through All Minds it is learning with organisers what helps most.

### What do attendees need?

Their own phone and a browser. They scan the QR code on screen or open the session link, then pick a language; to listen, they use their own earbuds. There’s no app.

### Can attendees catch up after a session?

Yes. Takeaways and summaries stay open, so people who stepped out or missed the session can catch up. Transcript downloads come with Pro.

### Can remote attendees follow too?

Yes. They open the same session link and follow in their language, wherever they are.

### What accessibility features are free?

Live captions and text translation, for every event: every room at once, up to 10 languages per session, 100 sessions a year. Voice translation is $10 per language, per session, with captions included. Takeaways, the Idea Cloud and summaries come with Pro at $249 per session, less in packs.

### What is All Minds?

A Snapsight partnership that brings Snapsight to events built around neuroinclusion, at subsidised or no cost. In return, you help learn what actually helps, and Snapsight shares it with the industry, with your consent.

## Who All Minds is for.

Organisations where neuroinclusion is central to the mission. Free live text is already on every plan; All Minds goes further.

[How Snapsight supports every attendee](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/accessibility)

**Accessibility and neurodiversity organisations**

Associations and non-profits focused on disability, accessibility or neurodivergent communities.

**Healthcare organisations**

Events for neurodivergent patients, caregivers, or the professionals who work with them.

**Education and research**

Conferences on inclusive education, universal design or cognitive accessibility.

**Events that put cognitive access first**

Any gathering designed with different minds in mind, where inclusive delivery is a priority.

## What we want to learn together.

There’s no playbook yet. With your consent, we’ll publish what we learn: a practical guide, templates and anonymised examples.

Apply to All Minds

1. Which formats help most: summaries, structured notes, action lists or full transcripts?
2. What reduces cognitive load without oversimplifying the content?
3. How do language and format choices change engagement across audiences?
4. What does good neuroinclusive knowledge delivery at events look like?

## Apply to All Minds.

Tell us about your organisation, your events, the people you serve and the access needs you want to meet. We’ll follow up within 10 business days.

Prefer email, or can’t see the form? Write to us directly.

[allminds@snapsight.com](mailto:allminds@snapsight.com)

The enquiry form is unavailable right now.

[Email allminds@snapsight.com](mailto:allminds@snapsight.com)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the All Minds initiative?

A Snapsight partnership that brings Snapsight to events built around neuroinclusion, at subsidised or no cost depending on the situation. In return, you work alongside Snapsight to learn what actually helps, and with your consent it is shared with the industry.

### Who can apply to All Minds?

Organisations where neuroinclusion is central to the mission. That includes accessibility and neurodiversity organisations, healthcare events for neurodivergent people and the professionals who work with them, education and research conferences on inclusion, and any event that puts cognitive access first.

### What formats help neurodivergent attendees follow a talk?

There is no playbook yet, which is why All Minds exists. Snapsight gives each attendee four ways in: live text to read word by word, takeaways added as the speaker makes each point, an Idea Cloud to explore from the idea that interests them, and a summary to come back to.

### What do we have to share in return?

Work alongside Snapsight to learn what actually helps: which formats, what reduces cognitive load without oversimplifying, and how language and format choices change engagement. Anything published, such as a guide, templates or anonymised examples, is shared only with your consent.

### Is live text free without All Minds?

Yes. Live text translation is free on every Snapsight plan for every event. All Minds goes further, for events where neuroinclusion is central.

### How do we apply?

Use the application form on the All Minds page, or email allminds@snapsight.com. Tell Snapsight about your organisation, your events, the people you serve and the access needs you want to meet, and it follows up within 10 business days.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can an AV company or agency resell Snapsight?

Yes. Snapsight agrees packages and wholesale rates with you, so your team can add it to quotes and order forms like any other line. Attendees see Snapsight alongside your client’s event branding, and Snapsight’s team works with yours on event day.

### What’s the difference between reselling and white label?

Resellers put Snapsight on their own quotes at wholesale rates, and attendees see Snapsight alongside the event’s branding. With white label, attendees see your brand instead of ours.

### Can we white-label Snapsight completely?

Yes. Full white label removes “Powered by Snapsight” from what attendees see and runs on your own domain or subdomain. It’s part of Enterprise; your event branding is included on paid plans.

### What can carry our brand?

Your logo, colours and fonts go on the event page, the attendee view and the stage screen, including the Idea Cloud background. You can remove the QR code and the “Powered by Snapsight” line, and run it on your own domain or subdomain. Reports and speaker cards carry your client’s event brand, as IAPCO’s and London Community Week’s do.

### Can it sit inside our clients’ event apps?

Yes. Snapsight works inside any event app, embedded as an iframe or opened from a link in the app’s own browser. The app team whitelists one link.

### Can we connect to your API?

Yes. Pull takeaways and reports into your own systems over the Snapsight API, or connect your AI assistant to your sessions over MCP.

### Do you support our events?

Yes. Before doors open Snapsight checks the audio feed and languages with your crew, and its team supports event day with you.

### How are partner rates set?

Tell Snapsight your clients, your events and your yearly volume, and it proposes rates for your quotes. Enterprise includes wholesale options for AV and production partners.

### Is our clients’ content secure?

Snapsight is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified, and GDPR compliant. Your content is never used to train AI models, and your data, and the IP in it, belongs to you.

Title: AI Innovation Asia 2024: Same-Day Highlights | Snapsight

[Customer stories](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/resources/case-studies/)

The Economist logo

**AI Innovation Asia 2024** Economist Impact Pan Pacific Singapore

# Session highlights the same day, not 48 hours later.

Economist Impact gave 500 executives summaries of every session by QR code, with real-time translation.

[Book a demo](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/contact?interest=takeaways) [Start free](https://www.snapsight.com/signup)

![A full ballroom at Economist Impact’s AI Innovation Asia 2024 in Singapore](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/assets/economist-room-BA2ORsMI.webp)

## The story

### The challenge

Economist Impact wanted attendees to leave with short summaries of in-depth discussions they could put to work, instead of waiting for edited recordings.

### What they ran

After validation by The Economist Group’s global teams: session summaries opened by QR codes on the LED walls and around the exhibition, with real-time translation.

### What happened

Highlights went out on the same day, where edited recordings could take up to 48 hours. Delegates gave excellent feedback, and staff and moderators used the summary links to recap.

## The numbers that mattered.

**500**

executives, corporate leaders and AI professionals

**Same day**

for session highlights, against up to 48 hours for edited recordings

> “The real-time translation and accuracy were impressive, and the summaries were immediately available after each session for delegates to access via QR code.”

**Organising team** Economist Impact

## What it looked like on the day.

![Delegates at a table in the networking area at AI Innovation Asia 2024, beside a QR code card for the event agenda](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/assets/economist-qr-card-ChjLYuUX.webp) ![An attendee photographs a panel on her phone at AI Innovation Asia 2024](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/assets/economist-phone-DArU0J7M.webp)

Title: The Decarbonised Mine: A Weekend, Not Weeks | Snapsight

[Customer stories](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/resources/case-studies/)

**The Decarbonised Mine** Andrew Slavin and team 2025 · Perth

# Weeks of post-event work, finished over a weekend.

A two-day mining conference replaced its record-edit-transcribe-write-design routine with summaries and reports from Snapsight.

[Book a demo](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/contact?interest=takeaways) [Start free](https://www.snapsight.com/signup)

![A speaker on stage at The Decarbonised Mine with presentation screens either side](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/assets/decarbonised-mine-stage-DooRa5NU.webp)

## The story

### The challenge

The team runs everything in-house. After each event they recorded every session, edited the videos, transcribed them, briefed a journalist and designed the reports. It took weeks, sometimes months.

### What they ran

Snapsight on both days of parallel sessions: a summary after every session by QR code, then post-event reports. The AV team had never used Snapsight and set it up without trouble.

### What happened

Attendees scanned the QR codes after every session without being told how, and the post-event work was done over the weekend. Snapsight is now the team’s default.

## The numbers that mattered.

**500+**

mining industry professionals over two days

**1 weekend**

for work that used to take weeks, sometimes months

> “The whole process that used to take us weeks was just… finished.”

**Andrew Slavin** Leads the team behind The Decarbonised Mine

Title: Tech Week Singapore 2024: 500+ Sessions Covered | Snapsight

[Customer stories](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/resources/case-studies/)

![Tech Week Singapore logo](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/assets/techweek-logo-BWOiTjJf.webp)

**Tech Week Singapore 2024** Tech Week Singapore Singapore

# 17 stages, 500+ sessions. 13,773 content views.

QR codes on all 17 stages gave 26,000+ attendees the takeaways from sessions they couldn’t reach.

[Book a demo](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/contact?interest=takeaways) [Start free](https://www.snapsight.com/signup)

![Tech Week Singapore 2024 stage with Snapsight QR codes on screens either side](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/assets/tech-week-stage-Deio9RgG.webp)

## The story

### The challenge

500+ sessions in two days across 17 stages, for 26,000+ attendees and 550+ international speakers. Attendees missed valuable content, organisers struggled to track engagement across the stages, and any fix had to work in real time without adding work for speakers or attendees.

### What they ran

QR codes on all 17 stages, one scan from each session’s takeaways. Snapsight Premium went further for attendees, surfacing the trends, opportunities, challenges and sentiment from the sessions they missed.

### What happened

1,540 active users viewed session insights 13,773 times, about nine views each, spending 3m 27s on average. Organisers saw in real time which sessions sparked the most interest, and Tech Week Singapore plans to run Snapsight again.

## The numbers that mattered.

**13,773**

content views across sessions

**1,540**

active users, 9 views each on average

**3m 27s**

average engagement time

> “They now get AI generated summaries of each of our conference sessions… It enables them to see every single session without actually being there as well.”

**Georgie May** CloserStill, Tech Week Singapore 2024 On camera at the show

## What it looked like on the day.

![Georgie May of CloserStill speaking at the Snapsight stand at Tech Week Singapore 2024](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/assets/tech-week-booth-DSCo3fol.webp)

Tech Week Singapore 2024 · a still from the video in the published story

Title: CityDNA Conference 2025: 65% Used It, Team of 4 | Snapsight

**CityDNA International Conference 2025** CityDNA 9–11 April 2025 · Budapest

of attendees used Snapsight

people on the organising team

Title: London Community Week 2026: 147 LinkedIn Posts | Snapsight

[Customer stories](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/resources/case-studies/)

![Community Week logo](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/assets/community-week-logo-DEZTMyp5.webp)

**London Community Week 2026** Led by Community C.I.C. 7–9 July 2026 · Big Penny Social, London

# 49 speakers. 147 LinkedIn posts.

A card for every speaker, shared across three official Pages for weeks after the event.

[Book a demo](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/contact?interest=speaker-remix) [Start free](https://www.snapsight.com/signup)

![A grid of Speaker Remix cards from London Community Week 2026](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/assets/london-cw-cards-WBGU1OdK.webp)

## The story

### The challenge

49 speakers covered everything from community-led growth to member retention. Turning those sessions into social posts by hand means watching every talk back, pulling lines, writing captions and making cards, then doing it again for two more official Pages, on a lean team already moving on to the next event.

### What they ran

As an event partner of London Community Week 2026, Snapsight ran Speaker Remix across the full roster: a card for every speaker with their name, their key point and the event’s identity, including its headline sponsor. The 49 stories went out on three official Pages, London Community Week, Community Week and Led by Community C.I.C., and the 48th speaker got the same care as the opening keynote.

### What happened

147 official LinkedIn posts drew 450+ visible engagements, an estimated 20,000 views and 48 reposts into new networks. Speakers’ ideas kept showing up in feeds for weeks after the event.

## The numbers that mattered.

**147**

official LinkedIn posts from 49 speaker stories

**450+**

visible engagements across three Pages

**48**

reposts into new networks

> “What impressed me most was how easy Remix made it for speakers themselves to jump in. Combined with our social team generating endless variations from each session, we kept London Community Week 2026’s momentum alive for weeks afterward.”

**Francisco Opazo** London Community Week

## 49 speakers, 49 cards.

Six of the 49 Speaker Remix cards · London Community Week 2026

Title: The Meetings Show 2025: All 65 Sessions Covered | Snapsight

[Customer stories](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/resources/case-studies/)

![The Meetings Show logo](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/assets/meetings-show-logo-BOa5ll7H.webp)

**The Meetings Show 2025** Northstar Travel Group ExCeL London

# Three stages at once. Every attendee got all 65 sessions.

Live text, key takeaways and Idea Clouds for every session on three main stages, readable in 99 languages.

[Book a demo](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/contact?interest=takeaways) [Start free](https://www.snapsight.com/signup)

![Idea Cloud from The Meetings Show 2025 session on talent and workforce development in the events industry](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/assets/tms-2025-idea-cloud-Byb6v_tF.webp)

## The story

### The challenge

Three stages ran at the same time. The 1,500 planners attending could physically get to perhaps 8–10 of the 65 sessions, and language kept international attendees from following all of it.

### What they ran

Live text, key takeaways and Idea Clouds for every session across the three main stages, opened in the browser in one click and readable in 99 languages. Setup took under five minutes, with no extra equipment.

### What happened

Attendees went from 8–10 sessions to all 65. Northstar Travel Group is expanding its Snapsight integration for 2026, exploring workshops, exhibitor presentations and specialised tracks.

## The numbers that mattered.

**65**

sessions open to every attendee, up from the 8–10 one person could attend

**99**

languages attendees could read them in

**<5 min**

total setup time for all 65 sessions

> “Instead of anxiously rushing between rooms, attendees were making strategic choices about where to spend their time, knowing nothing would be lost.”

**Emily Roberts** Senior Marketing Manager, Northstar Travel Group

## What it looked like on the day.

- ![Opening page of The Meetings Show 2025 Playbook, crediting Snapsight for capturing 65 live sessions](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/assets/tms-2025-playbook-D4JPLoz-.webp)
  
  Playbook · The Meetings Show 2025

Title: IMEX Frankfurt 2024: Summaries for 150+ Sessions | Snapsight

[Customer stories](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/resources/case-studies/)

IMEX logo

**IMEX Frankfurt 2024** IMEX Frankfurt

# 150+ education sessions, without leaving the show floor.

Summaries and Idea Clouds for every education session, inside the IMEX app and one scan from each room.

[Book a demo](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/contact?interest=takeaways) [Start free](https://www.snapsight.com/signup)

![Attendees around the giant IMEX letters on the IMEX Frankfurt 2024 show floor](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/assets/imex-frankfurt-floor-DXNX6ogg.webp)

## The story

### The challenge

IMEX wanted attendees to get the insights from 150+ education sessions, across tracks from Technology & Innovation to Well-being and Impact, without giving up time on the show floor. Reporting on them meant staff sitting in sessions and compiling notes by hand.

### What they ran

Real-time summaries and Idea Clouds for each education session, inside the IMEX Events app, linked from every session description and from QR codes at each room entrance. Pre-show communications told participants about it before the event began.

### What happened

Highlights from 150+ sessions went into post-event reporting automatically, with emerging trends and practical strategies for event professionals. IMEX’s own team recommended the summaries on LinkedIn.

## The numbers that mattered.

**150+**

education sessions summarised

**12,059**

participants with access in the IMEX app

**4,216**

buyers from 96 countries

> “It’s difficult for me to attend many of the amazing educational sessions that we run at IMEX. So, I’m grateful this year that we’re using AI… I think these are pretty good and you can access them from the IMEX app.”

**Carina Bauer** CEO, IMEX Group On LinkedIn, shown in the published story

Title: PCMA Convening Leaders 2024: 2,000 Users | Snapsight

[Customer stories](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/resources/case-studies/)

**PCMA Convening Leaders 2024** Professional Convention Management Association 7–10 January 2024 · San Diego Convention Center

# 5,000 attendees. 2,000 of them used Snapsight.

Real-time summaries and Idea Clouds, including for the Clinton keynote, with takeaways in seven languages.

[Book a demo](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/contact?interest=takeaways) [Start free](https://www.snapsight.com/signup)

![Convening Leaders 2024 stage with an Idea Cloud and QR code on the big screen](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/assets/pcma-cl-stage-M2g2h1sG.webp)

## The story

### The challenge

A record 5,000 business events professionals and a packed programme, with keynotes from Bill Clinton and Hillary Rodham Clinton, Mayim Bialik, Mo Gawdat and Nina Schick. PCMA wanted to help attendees distil and keep the key insights from each session, above all the high-profile keynotes.

### What they ran

Real-time AI summaries and Idea Clouds, opened by QR code, with takeaways in seven languages for an international audience: English, Spanish, Italian, French, German, Portuguese and Chinese.

### What happened

40% of attendees, 2,000 of 5,000, used Snapsight during the event. At the Clinton keynote, people could stay in the moment knowing they could revisit the main takeaways afterwards.

## The numbers that mattered.

**40%**

of attendees used it: 2,000 of 5,000

**7**

languages for every takeaway

> “That AI summary is really awesome, so useful when you are inundated with so much information & stimuli at live events.”

Title: ICCA Congress 2024: 60+ Sessions Summarised | Snapsight

[Customer stories](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/resources/case-studies/)

ICCA logo

**ICCA Congress 2024** ICCA ICC Abu Dhabi

# 60+ sessions summarised. The whole congress on one screen.

Live takeaways for every session and an event-wide Idea Cloud on a four-sided display hung over the venue.

[Book a demo](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/contact?interest=takeaways) [Start free](https://www.snapsight.com/signup)

![Four-sided LED display suspended over the ICCA Congress 2024 floor, showing the event-wide Idea Cloud](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/assets/icca-idea-cloud-cube-BDdk6h8r.webp)

## The story

### The challenge

Five simultaneous stages over four days, and most sessions aren’t recorded because there are so many. Without a record, the content was gone when the mics went off.

### What they ran

Live takeaways for every session in ICCA’s app, and an event-wide Idea Cloud on a four-sided LED display suspended in the centre of the venue: takeaways during sessions, the congress’s themes between them. The Idea Cloud began with a question from Ksenjia Polla of the ICCA team: could people see, in real time, what the whole event was talking about?

### What happened

Over 60% of attendees engaged with the content through the app, and the cloud showed what was trending live: sustainability, intergenerational engagement, AI. A full post-event report built from the live dialogue went to attendees, and ICCA planned to run Snapsight at every ICCA event in 2025.

## The numbers that mattered.

**60+**

sessions summarised

**60%+**

of attendees engaged with the content in the app

**5**

simultaneous stages over four days

## What it looked like on the day.

![A session hall at ICCA Congress 2024 in Abu Dhabi](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/assets/icca-hall-D9VDL2gs.webp)

ICCA Congress 2024 · from the published story

Title: IMEX America 2024: Session Takeaways in the App | Snapsight

[Customer stories](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/resources/case-studies/)

IMEX logo

**IMEX America 2024** IMEX Las Vegas

# 15,800 participants. Session takeaways in the IMEX app.

Session takeaways in the IMEX app for a show with 15,800 participants and 85,000 meetings.

[Book a demo](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/contact?interest=takeaways) [Start free](https://www.snapsight.com/signup)

## The story

### The challenge

IMEX America drew 15,800 participants, including 5,758 buyers from 75 countries, and 3,500+ exhibiting companies, with 85,000 meetings on the floor. Attendees had little time for sessions, and the ones they wanted often clashed.

### What they ran

After its debut in the IMEX Frankfurt app, Snapsight returned inside the IMEX app with session takeaways, plus Snapsight Premium: deeper AI analysis, personalised intelligence reports for attendees and organisers, and monitoring tools for data-driven decisions.

### What happened

Attendees used the Snapsight notes to catch up on sessions they couldn’t get to, with key takeaways in the app for the majority of sessions.

## The numbers that mattered.

**15,800**

participants

**5,758**

buyers from 75 countries

**85,000**

meetings competing with the education programme

> “We’re helping attendees maximize show time by providing quick, accessible session insights while delivering high-level intelligence for global event planners.”

**Gary Coombs** COO, IMEX

## What people at the event said about it.

> “Thanks to Snapsight, there are key takeaways for the majority in the app… I spent all my time on the IMEX Inspiration Hub and still saw only a fraction of the content.”

**Tahira Endean** Event expert

> “There were always at least two sessions I wanted to attend at the same time. Love that I can look at the Snapsight notes for the sessions I missed.”

**Ephi Maglaris** Event strategist

## The story

### The challenge

UFI first ran Snapsight at its Asia Pacific Conference in Macau in March 2024, for nearly 300 delegates from 20 countries and regions. For the European Conference in June, it wanted the highlights inside its own conference app, so delegates wouldn’t have to go to a separate platform.

### What they ran

Key takeaways in the conference mobile app for 300 delegates from 41 countries and regions, across main-stage sessions, breakout discussions and the Event Director Summit. UFI’s tech team added them to the app themselves, with no code.

### What happened

Snapsight is now part of UFI’s event programming and standard operating procedure. The post-event report, with session takeaways and sentiment analysis, feeds UFI’s strategic planning.

## The numbers that mattered.

**300**

delegates from 41 countries and regions

**3 months**

from a first try in Macau to standard

**No code**

to put takeaways in the UFI app

> “I was very happy to introduce Snapsight into the European Conference. It was really easy to integrate into our mobile app which I think made all the difference. As opposed to delegates having to navigate to a separate platform, they could check out the highlights instantly in the app.”

**Nick Dugdale-Moore** Regional Director – Europe, UFI

Title: The Meetings Show APAC: Takeaways to White Paper | Snapsight

**The Meetings Show APAC 2024** Northstar Travel Group 17–18 April 2024 · Marina Bay Sands, Singapore

# 23 main-stage sessions. One white paper for everyone else.

Takeaways flashed on screen after every main-stage session, then shared with the whole community as a white paper.

[Book a demo](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/contact?interest=takeaways) [Start free](https://www.snapsight.com/signup)

## The story

### The challenge

The first Meetings Show APAC, at Marina Bay Sands, wanted to give attendees an immersive, engaging experience, and to get its main-stage content to the wider community who couldn’t travel to Singapore.

### What they ran

Snapsight captured all 23 main-stage sessions with no extra setup and produced key takeaways and Idea Clouds. Northstar built it into the programme: at the end of each session the host or MC highlighted the takeaways and invited attendees to scan the QR code.

### What happened

The takeaways sparked discussion in the room. After the show, Northstar and Snapsight turned the insights into a white paper, Asia Pacific’s role in recasting the global MICE sector, and sent it to the whole community by newsletter.

## The numbers that mattered.

**23**

main-stage sessions captured, with no extra setup

**David Blansfield** Executive Vice President and Group Publisher, Northstar Travels

**James Lancaster** AMI Editor & Editorial Director, Northstar Meetings Group – UK

> “Not only was it a value add for the experience in person but as a media provider, one who obviously cares for the community that we serve at large, we are taking that content.”

> “The seemingly effortless way in which the show’s content is summarized and delivered provides a real-world example of the region’s influence in providing next-generation solutions…”

**BEIA Conference & AGM 2024** Business Events Industry Aotearoa New Plymouth

# One volunteer ran it for the whole conference.

After a 15-minute test at home, one volunteer ran Snapsight for 170 industry leaders.

[Book a demo](https://www.snapsight.com/snapsight-website-preview/contact?interest=takeaways) [Start free](https://www.snapsight.com/signup)

## The story

### The challenge

Content capture relied on delegates’ own notes, and BEIA had no business case for recording every session. The AV team was wary of learning a new system in a short time.

### What they ran

Snapsight, run by a single volunteer, with QR codes on the screens at the venue entrances and during breaks, information sheets on the tables and links in the conference app.

### What happened

Delegates stayed present instead of taking notes, and BEIA kept the content to show what people missed and to promote future years.
